title: Ops Shortcut Builder: convert incident transcripts into safe, parameterized runflow tasks
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: Oncall engineers frequently triage incidents using Slack/Zoom threads and then codify runbook steps ad-hoc into scripts. This process is slow, error-prone, and difficult to review. Goal: provide a tool that ingests incident transcripts (chat logs, Zoom captions, incident notes) and proposes idempotent, typed 'shortcut' tasks (micro-runflows) that operators can review, test in a sandbox, and publish to the runbook catalog. The output must enforce permission gating, inject telemetry hooks, include dry-run safety checks, and produce Git-backed artifacts (task definitions + test harness).
acceptance_criteria: Tool accepts transcripts (.md, .txt, exported Slack thread) and returns a candidate task bundle within 60s for a 10k word transcript
Generated tasks have typed inputs, default safe values, and explicit permission checks in metadata
Tasks run in a sandboxed dry-run mode that records intent-only telemetry without making destructive changes
Operators can edit the suggested steps in the UI and re-run validation which produces a deterministic diffable artifact in the git task catalog
Telemetry surface shows per-step estimated blast radius, token-cost estimate for any embedded LLM calls, and recommended telemetry events
End-to-end UX documented and tested with 3 pilot incidents and 2 oncall engineers providing sign-off
comments: 2025-08-11 Priya Nair: Kicked off discovery. Pulled 5 anonymized incident transcripts from last quarter (pager/root-cause threads). Initial manual mapping shows ~70% of steps are repetitive and easily parameterizable.

2025-08-14 Ethan Brooks: Spike complete. Built a prototype that identifies step boundaries using cue phrases and timestamps. Prototype outputs a YAML task schema with inputs and a safety flag. Found tricky cases where human action is required (credentials rotation) — those must be surfaced as 'manual step' with explicit escalation links.
2025-08-16 Design feedback (Maya Chen): Suggested inline safety annotations and a compact UI diff view for step edits. Need copy for operators explaining dry-run semantics and permission gating UX.

2025-08-18 Engineering note: We should reuse existing task schema from ENG-761451 to maintain compatibility with the runbook runtime. Will add a small adapter to map our generated schema to the canonical format.

2025-08-20 Security review (Jordan Lee): Reviewed threat model. Require KMS-backed credential references and disallow credential exfiltration in generated steps. Flagged requirement for audit logs on publish and on-run. Marked security_review_required = true.

2025-08-22 QA (Asha Verma): Built sandbox harness. Dry-run mode correctly prevented mutation for 12/12 sample actions. Found flaky behavior for a step invoking opsctl where network timeouts were treated as success — fixed retry semantics and idempotency checks.

2025-08-24 PM (Liam O'Connor): PO review. Agreed MVP scope: transcript ingestion + generated task with editor + sandbox dry-run + publish to git catalog. Defer automation suggestion engine and telemetry scorer to follow-up.

2025-08-25 Ethan Brooks: Open PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-shortcuts/pull/74. Draft UI in Console playground at console.internal/redwood/ops-shortcuts. Next: run pilot with security-approved transcripts and iterate on blast radius estimator.
next_steps: Run pilot with 2 oncall teams (schedule: 2025-08-28 to 2025-09-04)
Complete security checklist and add KMS credential reference handling
Add adapter that emits canonical task YAML compatible with runbook runtime
Add e2e test: transcript -> generated task -> dry-run -> publish commit
